CHIEF COMPLAINT
Evaluation of kidneys in patient with Smith-Magenis syndrome.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Katherine is a 22-month-old former 34 and 3/7 week twin presenting for nephrology evaluation. Patient was born at 4 pounds 8 ounces with her twin sister weighing 3 pounds 13 ounces. In the neonatal period, she had feeding difficulties with apneic episodes during feeding and temperature dysregulation. She has been followed by gastroenterology for severe reflux, has been on a cow's milk-free diet per dietician recommendation, and has been evaluated by allergy and neurology. Patient was diagnosed with Smith-Magenis syndrome by geneticist after failure to sit by herself by one year of age and not yet walking. She is now crawling and attempting to take steps. Currently enrolled in multiple therapies including feeding therapy, occupational therapy, physical therapy, and starting speech therapy within the next couple of weeks. Has also been evaluated by orthopedics, ophthalmology, and audiology. Voids approximately 8-10 wet diapers per 24-hour period and has good fluid intake with ripple pea protein milk, water, and occasional dilute juice. Twin sister is doing well and developmentally appropriate. Family presenting today to ensure kidney health is normal given reported association of Smith-Magenis syndrome with congenital kidney and urinary tract anomalies.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Good fluid intake. Normal voiding pattern with 8-10 wet diapers daily. Patient appears to drink well. No concerning urinary symptoms reported.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Smith-Magenis syndrome (chromosomal deletion)
Prematurity (born 34 and 3/7 weeks)
Neonatal feeding difficulties with apnea during feeding
Neonatal temperature dysregulation
Severe gastroesophageal reflux disease
Cow's milk intolerance
Developmental delay (not sitting by one year, now crawling and attempting steps)

MEDICATIONS
Not documented in conversation.

ALLERGIES
Cow's milk intolerance.

FAMILY HISTORY
Older brother (9 years old) with autism. Twin sister healthy and developmentally normal. No family history of kidney failure, dialysis, or transplantation.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Lives in Dallas, Georgia. Currently enrolled in multiple therapeutic services.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Well-nourished female, slightly fussy during examination. Eyes small appearing. Mild hypotonia of lower extremities and arms. Normal external female genitalia. Heart and lungs normal. Ears normal.

RESULTS
Pending renal ultrasound.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
22-month-old former 34 and 3/7 week twin with Smith-Magenis syndrome presenting for renal screening. Smith-Magenis syndrome is a chromosomal deletion syndrome that can affect multiple organ systems. Congenital anomalies of the kidney and urinary tract have been reported in association with this condition. Plan includes renal ultrasound today to screen for kidney abnormalities. If ultrasound is normal, patient will not require follow-up with nephrology. If ultrasound is abnormal, will determine next steps and arrange follow-up at town center location in Kennesaw area. Results will be communicated to family.
